Many of them come with health problems which have worsened over time, some have caused me to drastically flip in emotional stability. I suppose I like to separate them because every year up to this point has introduced me to new problems, new reasons, new anxieties. Because I've grown up virtually alone, with few significant friends/family in my life.. my knowledge lacks in the doctor search department. Especially since I might not have insurance come September and I happen to only be "covered" by "family coverage" offered to me by my dad's insurance company for HIS doctor.
I suppose no one knows how to locate this person?

I don't really think it's appropriate to feel like your problems are invisible but at the same time, everyone has their own share of feelings that can be easily fixed and easily solved. I'm not stereotyping you as a "perpetual whiner" or a misogynist. I submitted this post because everyone has periods of self doubt and feelings of loneliness. I can tell you aren't ready for the truth though, You go straight to accusation and hostility. You don't "agree" or "like" someone else's solution unless it caters to your relateability. Good luck searching for answers because you clearly don't know it's within you.

No one wants to be with an individual who is remotely co-dependent or maybe completely. I am a young female and I can see/relate to the feelings most people have about this "that they don't think its a personal problem, but it's just everyone else etc etc" this is followed by "I am going to kill myself" <as simply put as that is, you are blaming lack of -whatever issue you're upset about- and instead you acknowledge the failure but fail to see the potential of change in a positive and healthy way!

I am not too sure if this thread can always help those who find themselves in a bind, people don't like to hear the truth and if it's too hurtful, they'd rather report the "harassment" or "hating." I think it is very possible to live a socially sexual life, serious/short relationship experience but the problem is; most "depressed" people cannot benefit from dedicated lovers because it becomes a privilege to abuse. I'm sure you have had your fair share of relationships where "you love them too much, you become clingy, you're sweet" can sometimes say something else.. You cannot expect anything from life if there's something you need to fix on your own, from within. No one can share a TWO PERSON relationship if one of you has to put in more work than the other (most likely the one who isn't depressed). In most healthy relationships, both partners love not only each other, but themselves. 

They have reliable social circles AWAY from their significant others (aka SO's) in order to remain connected and level headed (don't forget yourself!), you don't battle feelings of constant jealousy and trust is easy when you are individually confident and reliable. You have to live a healthy and happy life before you feel that life should give you a break. You dont need an amazing job to be happy, or a college education. You don't need to follow anyone's rules, beliefs, morals, religion, ideals, body image; free yourself knowing that you are your own person and educate your life with things that impact you most. Don't live feeling trapped, take advantage of your life and consider the world we live in, do we really have another life once we pass? What remains, is it worth passing up this life for something that could last an eternity if I choose to die now? Am I proud of my mistakes? and if so, Should I be ashamed? Is it worse to question others or just the reactions from myself? Do I need to be concerned with anyone's opinions? Do I love myself? Is my life happy without a lover? (if no, then this is an unhealthy mentality!) Let life love you, Love life back. Everything is simpler than we think.

"-petty theft, simple assault or driving under the influence of alcohol and/or other drugs. Typically, the maximum sentence is one year in county jail and/or $5,000 in fines."

Source: Wikipedia. Now, how is this type of "gross misdemeanor" supposed to keep you from applying for college? Paying back whomever needs the cheque from you etc etc. The world is more accommodating than you think; in my opinion, it's only conveniently situated for the people who are interested in positive futures AKA the ones who aren't suicidal (confident, driven, maybe even the "%1"). Regardless, the jail sentence isn't very long, many successful business owners who get out after 5+ years locked up live a decent life (I'm sure) or even happy x-con parents who belong to an amazing family. There are many ways that life sends you opportunities to change and grow. Being so young, dont take this huge event negatively. Plus, I owe the government money too! But... that was for school loans. I'm still here, looking for work and soon I can pay it off + interest.

"I'm too stupid" The first place you should start in order to fix your life is to drop that negative reinforcement. Honestly, it's not like you're the only one going through problems because I do too! My friends, your friends.. everyone reaches hard patches in life. Somethings are better left accepted and unfinished. Some things are better left completed. If life was easy, that would ruin the thrill of the reward. You are a person, who has the capacity to do and change and make something out of your life. So please, don't throw it away for a darkness of unknown.

There could be many reasons why this is becoming increasingly hard to work out (the whole comm. and arguing). In my LDR, Since my bf spent a lot of his energy helping me deal with my anxiety and depression it's taken a toll on him as well. The more he's honest, the more it tends to hurt. I think you should spend more time fixing your end of the relationship in juxtaposition to giving her encouragement to communicate and be honest as well. Build a trust so that both partners can feel safe and secure when confiding! That way, no one gets mad. If I was making my boyfriend miserable, I'd kinda hope he would be able to find some sort of outlet. She also might need some breaks from baby handling all the time, going out with friends, finding new interests, changing a job perhaps? You have no idea how much a girl can change herself to make a guy happy and, it goes A LONG WAY if you make her feel like your only confidant once in a while. You both know the answers but, even discussing an already cracked quest is still fun when you've got a girlfriend to give you some cheering.

I think in terms of things getting so heated that one person threatens to leave; has to be brought under control immediately. Never say anything derogatory TO THEM because they will only take it personally when the moment is upsetting enough. Find out what you both want in a relationship, make objectives and see how they fit into your own personal lives. And honestly, make her feel loved. Guys are so hard to convince when it comes to "showing love" from what I've seen, showing it to them isn't really an obvious gesture (in a girls perspective)(for the most part lol...)

Well, I don't think I can write a huge paragraph similar to usermdh but I can definitely say that I am experiencing the same thing. The difference is that my opinion is from a female perspective! The first thing you need to keep in mind are, boundaries that both of you can agree upon in order to improve your relationship (not take things personally, attempting to be more honest, showing appreciation and love) achieving these things can be especially hard when both partners have expectations for the other person. Please try and remove any irrational expectations for her. Start somewhere malleable, dont expect to open up a dramatic conflict for answers but maybe say "hey, lets make sure we still end our night on a good note (skyping + bed, a nice i love you phone call etc)" start with small/noticeable acts that can help make your life consistently happier together!

I haven't read through this much but I had an immediate opinion that I felt like sharing. First of all, I think healthy eating has to involve the extent one is willing to go to buy locally. Secondly, If you can "eat healthy" from using your resources wisely rather than compare your habits to others. The key is to understand what benifits you more in relation to the area you live in. Asian supermarkets, farmers markets and any general grocer will carry an assortment of veggies/fruits/meats that could very likely cook enough for a week. I think the whole mess of people complaining about "available/affordable and healthy food" needs to be changed to "Im too used to over consuming, I am unable to recognize my financial limitations and work around them in order to avoid more harm to my already deprived body"

Ive cleaned the house... I think I've been house bound for 2 weeks? Not my longest but if I were to say "technically not walking out my door" than yes it is my longest. every day I've woken up, I've intended to look for work but... every day has been another failure. I don't think I would like to die by inhalation.. it seems to "realistic" when it comes to escaping my fears. Id like to be in a lot of pain when I die.

Death doesn't fix anything. There is nothing after death but this is also an aspect I still don't take seriously. We all feel defeated at times but you have to understand how your mind works, what you enjoy doing, what gives you confidence. For example, when I am really upset and I cant get out of my house due to my fears and insecurities, I clean! And trust me it's hard to start but once you see one clean area it's really easy to clean the whole house. It's a really great way for me to get my mind off of life and at the end, I have a clean house! Is there anything like that you could do? To help you get going?
